description: Outcome: during the internal launch, the request-access form accepts only invited people, enforced by the application, not by an unadvertised URL. Builds: a setting that names the launch mode; single-use, expiring invitation tokens issued by an owner-run command (never by a model or a routine operator), bound to the invited address; uninvited submissions get the same uniform response as any other refusal (no enumeration); the mode is visible in the dossier and the health report; turning it off is a recorded owner act. Non-goals: a public waiting list, a second intake form. Authority class: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: the internal launch. design: Design (Django review 2026-10-23): validate the mode at start-up in the guards (default closed; refuse an environment-sourced value); enforce the check inside the intake service's transaction, consuming the invitation with a conditional UPDATE; prefer an address-bound invitation row on the existing email key plus the existing mail confirmation over a bearer token (a token would need redaction, a proxy route and private-header handling); state whether consumption happens at accept or at confirm (recommended: at confirm, so an unconfirmed submission does not burn the invitation).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: an uninvited address is refused with the same response and timing as every other refusal (unknown, expired, used and wrong-address cases indistinguishable); an invitation is single-use (concurrent redemption admits one) and expires; issuance is an owner-run command that writes an audit record; an unset or invalid mode value refuses start-up and the default is invitation-only; the mode is read from code-fixed configuration so the release receipt is the recorded owner act; a public intake with the mode off is byte-identical to today; the dossier and health report show the mode. title: Owner decision: replace the application role's DELETE on pause rows with a security-definer resume function, or accept code-level authorization for resume
description: Why: the security review of PR #88 (9kg.6) found that the database guard requires a same-transaction staff resume event but cannot tell an audited resume from one the application role forged by inserting the event itself; the decision-maker permission and the open-cause rule are enforced in code only. Options: (a) accept, with the limit recorded in 016 section 10.13 (done in PR #88); (b) revoke the app role's DELETE on the pause table and expose a SECURITY DEFINER resume function that writes the event, requires the note length and checks the open-cause rule in SQL. Authority: policy (owner or architect), then repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: none at launch.
acceptance_criteria: The owner's choice is recorded in 016 section 10.13; if (b), the function exists, the app role has no DELETE on the pause table, resume() calls the function, and the pause-guard tests cover the forged-event path being refused.
notes: 2026-10-26: the pause-guard limit is described in 016 section 10.15, not 10.13 as the description says. The owner decision package (031 section 4) recommends option (a) for the internal launch and revisiting (b) before wider enrollment.

title: Require occurred_at at or after the transaction timestamp in the three same-transaction txid guards so a restore onto a rebuilt cluster cannot reuse an old event
description: Why: the data review of PR #88 (9kg.6) found that a restore loads created_txid values from the old cluster; a fresh cluster's transaction id counter restarts low, so an old automation_resumed, decision or agreement event could equal a later transaction's id and satisfy the guard. The same weakness is in the assessments 0008 and agreements 0004 guards. Authority: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: the production restore drill under the host go.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three guards also requires the event's occurred_at to be at or after transaction_timestamp(); the restore drill proves a restored old event no longer satisfies a new transaction's guard; the reverse-and-reapply test counts stay consistent.

Narrow them to the provisioning step (step-level env in CI, an env prefix on provision_db_roles.py in compose) and pass the superuser-refusal probes their login another way, e.g. a dedicated probe-only variable. Deferred: not required by the owner's closeout text, which covers web and worker child processes.
